source_observations.locator: Sanskrit Library, Osmania edition index, 1.4.72 and 8.3.42
source_observations.observation: The two one-page scan files are indexed as p92 and p947. The second file shows the volume page number 295.

source_observations.locator: Osmania Kāśikā vol. I, printed p. 92, 1.4.72, main text
source_observations.observation: The concealment rule prints both lyap forms and, after participial and finite examples, tiraskṛtvā followed by tiraḥ kṛtvā. The wood example follows the restriction.

source_observations.locator: Same printed p. 92, apparatus note 1 linked to the ktvā example
source_observations.observation: The editors expressly question this arrangement of examples because evidence for s with a non-gati tiras is lacking on their analysis.

source_observations.locator: Osmania Kāśikā, vol. II, printed p. 295, file p947, 8.3.42, main text
source_observations.observation: Alternation of s and visarga in agent, infinitive and necessity examples precedes the explicit gati restriction and the non-gati ktvā counterexample.
The apparatus lists tiraskṛtvā under the printed siglum इ. in the vicinity of the non-gati control. The variant and the main text have separate documentary grades.
Preserves both ktvā displays. Their sequence puts the visarga form before the s form. The gati/lyap pair belongs earlier in the field.

source_observations.locator: Bhoja, Śṛṅgāraprakāśa, first chapter, indexed passage 648
source_observations.observation: The metalinguistic list under the numbered rule includes both ktvā spellings, with s first. This is a report of examples.

source_observations.locator: Pascale Haag and Vincenzo Vergiani, study of the Kāśikāvṛtti, introduction on the Osmania edition
source_observations.observation: Describes the negative apparatus and the need to check individual sources. The linked study treats the pratyāhāra section.
